notes.title: 🔥 Announcing tentative plans 🔥
notes.content:
Hey kids,

I just wanted you to know that I haven't forgotten about [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i].

Or, dare I say (yes- I do dare), haven't forgotten about [i]you[/i].

For by your very act of reading this text, yours and [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i]'s destiny are inexplicably intertwined.

That is to say, I remember you.

And by remembering you, I remember my promise.

Which was...
...
...
...
...euphoria.

Euphorically yours,
Josh Powlison
Creator of [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i]

PS- My tentative plans are that I will release an update at some point that I haven't decided on, with some features that I have ideas for.

PPS- Euphoria.

I want to be professional. It's the foundation for having a profession.

And nothing is more professional than Microsoft.

So I got a Business Premium license (because I think I'm worth it) and set up my new professional email address:

dad@thebutton.life

I wasn't able to work on the game more until I got this resolved. As I said, professionalism is the foundation for having a profession. While all those other game devs were wasting their time programming, QAing, and arting around, I've been setting myself up for success.

Euphorically yours,
Josh Powlison
Creator of [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i]

notes.title: Should we change BUTTON to be about LEVERS?!
notes.content:
I just had a startling thought. Maybe I've been making the wrong game all along.

I already made [i]BUTTON[/i]. You know what I [i]haven't[/i] made yet?

LEVER.

Why did I do [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i] first? Was this a mistake? Am I a fool?

No...
...no, I am merely misguided.

A lever is just a button, hidden behind a lever.

Isn't that right?

Yes, yes, yes.
Yes, yes, yes, yes, yes.
Yes yes.

It all comes back...
...to the BUTTON.

Euphoria.

Euphorically yours,
Josh Powlison
Creator of [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i]

notes.title: Maybe I'm trying too hard
notes.content:
Dear children,

I've wondered if the reason I haven't released any updates in a while is because I'm trying too hard.

You see, sometimes the better the effort, the [i]worse it actually is[/i]. I once had someone tell me "try harder, die younger." They told me this in a dream.

In the dream, I was trying to corral fish into a washing machine so they could become tuna fish sandwiches. I don't even like tuna fish sandwiches. But I think it was a metaphor for [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i].

You see, if I try harder, my dream may die younger. But if I release the gas a little, perhaps my passion will stay alive, and so will the project.

Therefore, I'm thinking of trying less hard.

What do you think? Do you think that will get us yet closer...
...to achieving...
...euphoria?

Let me know in the comments.

Euphorically yours,
Josh Powlison
Creator of [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i]

notes.title: I just met people who haven't heard of BUTTON (full title won't fit)
notes.content:
I was walking in the grocery store, wearing my [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i] onesie, and someone commented "oh, that's so cute and fabulous, what is that?"

i figured they would know. I figured it would be obvious.

But I went along, figuring they would know exactly what I was referring to. "Oh, it's a onesie for [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i]!" I replied cheerfully.

"What's that?"

My heart dropped. And so did my knees. When I finished screaming up at the ceiling, I turned my attention to the individual. "I apologize," I stated. "I lost my composure there for a moment."

I got up, and asked: "You... you haven't heard of [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i]?"

They shook their head.

"That's an agreement with my negative statement, correct?"

They thought for a second, then nodded.

It's a bad thing that happened in the Oreo aisle, because I ended up stocking up too much.

Now I'm crying into Oreos and milk. But they don't satisfy.

Only BUTTON satisfies.

Keep pressing on, my children.

Euphorically yours,
Josh Powlison
Creator of [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i]

notes.title: What would a BUTTON movie be like?
notes.content:
I was lying awake thinking about what we would do if this franchise suddenly took off. I figure we'd make a movie.

Street Fighter got a movie. Warcraft got a movie. Minecraft got a movie. Mario got a movie, and then another one. Metal Gear Solid got a movie (you know, Metal Gear Solid 4). So it's only natural that the natural evolution of video games is to become movies.

Because nothing is more exciting for players than to stop playing. It's like that feeling when you finally beat a video game, except you get that feeling the entire time. Incredible.

So anyway, here's a mockup of the poster that I envisioned:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031805/82cb32ababa9421b2c9d9b6ff878a196690c88b0.jpg[/img]

I'm guessing Morgan Freeman would voice over the whole thing, Dee Bradley Baker would voice the BUTTON, and I don't even know who the cool female actresses are anymore but one of them would probably be on the poster.

She's probably be in her house, alone, and one day she goes into work and finds out that her entire existence has been erased. Then, she's taken into a room where Morgan Freeman, government agent, explans a phenomenom- that happens quite rarely, but it's happened to her.

As he folds his hands and leans over the table, he tells her that this may seem like the end of a lifetime- but it's actually the chance of the lifetime.

I'll write out the next part of the scene so you can envision it:

MORGAN FREEMAN
Now, you have no name. You have no history. We only know one thing.

HEADLINING ACTRESS
What's that?

MORGAN FREEMAN
The button is calling you.

HEADLINING ACTRESS
What?

MORGAN FREEMAN
Your destiny, as it always has been, is no different than it ever has been.

HEADLINING ACTRESS
What are you talking about?

MORGAN FREEMAN
You see, Mrs. Nameless Woman-

[i]Morgan Freeman pulls out a suitcase, and opens it up. A series of wires are connected to a single red button.[/i]

MORGAN FREEMAN
-we have no idea what this button does. But no one in existence wants their name to be sullied with this thing if it happens to doom mankind. At the same time, we require the knowledge, because we have received detailed intel that implies this button may be mankind's salvation against the incoming alien invasion.

HEADLINING ACTRESS
What does this have to do with me? I'm just a humble Facebook Marketplace saleswoman.

MORGAN FREEMAN
I hate to break it to you, but you never even existed on Facebook. And if Zuck doesn't know you, then the government [i]definitely[/i] doesn't know you.

[i]Morgan Freeman takes a sip of Coca-Cola, who is definitely sponsoring this film. After all, they already missed out on ET and had to settle for Mac and Me, they should be an easy sell for this one.[/i]

MORGAN FREEMAN
We need someone who has nothing to lose to press this button. Someone who is unafraid of the risk, because they have no risk. Because they have no [i]thing[/i]. You are that person.

[i]Headlining Actress immediately presses the button.[/i]

MORGAN FREEMAN
Now, that was very bold of you.

HEADLINING ACTRESS
No it wasn't.

[i]Music begins to build.[/i]

MORGAN FREEMAN
Excuse me now?

HEADLINING ACTRESS
I've barely done anything. As a Facebook Marketplace saleswoman, I pressed more buttons than you've ever seen in your life. I've written more messages, flagged more spam, and blocked more weirdos than you've met in this interrogation chamber. Believe me, Mister- I know my buttons. No- what I did wasn't bold at all.

MORGAN FREEMAN
(laughs)
And what are you getting at?

HEADLINING ACTRESS
You see, Mister- pressing is only half of the process of activating a button...
...I have yet to release it.

[i]Music pulses.[/i]

MORGAN FREEMAN
Well I'll be.

[i]Morgan Freeman turns around and walks out the door, followed by two other agents.[/i]

MORGAN FREEMAN
Well, we're still waiting on her, I guess. Let's go get some chicken nuggets.

[i]The doors slam behind them. Headlining Actress is left alone with the button.[/i]

HEADLINING ACTRESS
(nervous, laughing, tears streaming down her face)
You know, I've always been accused of never finishing what I started.

///////////////////////

Anyway, yeah.

Do you think it would go similarly?

Who do you think would be the perfect currently-popular (or popular within the last 40 years, I dunno) actress for the [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition: The Movie[/i] movie?

I think it'd be the best movie since the Mario movie.

The first one, I mean.

Euphorically yours,
Josh Powlison
Creator of [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i]/Screenwriter

notes.title: I ate fried chicken recently
notes.content:
It was store-bought and kind of disappointing.

It wasn't crispy, even though I put it in the oven and followed the instructions. It didn't pull apart in a satisfying way. It was just kinda... there. Like an old doily that hasn't been washed in months.

I'm not as excited about it as I was before I wasn't excited about it.

But the good news is, I know where I can get good chicken nuggets.

So it's okay.

But I also need to figure out when I'm going to keep working on the game not just in my head, but also [i]with my hands[/i]. My hands are itching for coding, but my head is itching for my pillow. It's hard to find time to work when your head's so itchy.

The good news is though, that now that I have money from my job, I was able to go to a hair store and ask what could possibly be better than my 2-in-1 shampoo/conditioner. They gave me 1-in-2 shampoo/conditioner instead, and now my hair's starting to feel greasy for the first time in years. It's amazing.

So my head will probably be itching less soon. That's the point I'm trying to make.

Anyway, I just wanted to write that before my itchy head hits my itchy pillow.

Also, keep pressing the button. After all, there's nothing more urgent, nothing more pressing...
...than...
...euphoria.

Euphorically yours,
Josh Powlison
Creator of [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i]

notes.title: Terrible, awful, drastic news... (click to read it)
notes.content:
I have bad news.

It turns out that my work on BUTTON hasn't been enough to sustain my chicken nugget budget. Heck, I can't even afford [i]my home[/i].

This is a problem. Even though my landlord is my mom, I still need to pay her or else [i]she[/i] can't sustain [i]her[/i] chicken nugget budget. And if she doesn't get her money, [i]she[/i] can't pay [i]her taxes[/i], and then the mayor won't be able to sustain [i]their[/i] chicken nugget budget, and the economy will collapse.

So this is the bad news:

...
...
...
...I got a job.

That's right. It's defeat for any independent game developer. I did the one thing you're [b]NEVER SUPPOSED TO DO[/b]- went to the grind for "the man". "The man" in this case offered to pay me more than enough for chicken nuggets, [i]in addition[/i] to my home. That's a tough offer to pass up.

But it's also a tough pill to swallow. I used to spend all my time [i]thinking about working[/i], and now I'm spending all my time [i]working[/i]. As you might imagine, as a result of this my productivity has gone [b]way[/b] down.

Here's a graph to explain the concept:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031805/50dc04a583e843f080e2b063d4e943c1f6b5d7df.png[/img]

So now what?

Well, the good news is that I'll have more money to pour into the game.

The bad news is that I'll have [i]less time[/i].

I know you've come to expect regular updates. You've already gotten one, and your appetiate is whet. It's so whet, it's like a... like a whetstone. Like a whetstone... of anticipation. And we're sharpening our knives of excitement on this whetstone of anticipation, which is your appetite.

See, time is money. But I have less time. Therefore, even though I'm making more money, [i]it's almost like I'm making less money[/i]. It's just how the math works out.

So yeah. I'm coming forward and confessing. I got a job. I'm sorry I failed you all. I know this is [i]the last thing you wanted to hear[/i]- that I'll be able to feed myself, and maybe get a dog. But it's reality- [i]I got a job.[/i]

I'm sorry to you all. I have failed as a game developer. I have failed you all.

But...
...the BUTTON hasn't failed you.

Please remember to continue to press and release the button, my children.

And one day, you too...
...yes, even you, yes you in the back...
...will achieve...
...
...
........
..euphoria.

Euphorically yours,
Josh Powlison
Creator of [i]Josh Powlison's BUTTON: Mildly Remastered Edition[/i]/Worker for "The Man"
